title: Faithful curve actions have free geometric orbits
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $C$ by $F$-automorphisms. Suppose $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_F(C)$ is injective. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every extension field $E/F$, the pullbacks $C_E$ and $L_E$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback] have the following properties: $C_E$ is a smooth proper geometrically integral Noetherian curve of dimension one, $L_E$ is ample, and every finite locally free module on $C_E$ and every coherent ideal tensored with such a module is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Noetherian means quasi-compact and covered by affine spectra of Noetherian rings, and finite locally free means locally a finite direct sum of the structure sheaf. For every algebraic closure $\Omega/F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the induced action on $D=C_\Omega$ remains faithful and there is a nonempty open $D^\circ\subseteq D$ such that no nonidentity element fixes a geometric point of $D^\circ$. In particular there is an $\Omega$-rational closed point $x\in D^\circ$ and the points $gx$ for $g\in G$ are all distinct. This includes $G=\{1\}$; no restriction on the characteristic is assumed.

proof.text: Fix an extension $E/F$. Projectivity makes $C$ proper, and properness survives this base change; hence $C_E$ is separated, quasi-compact and of finite type over $E$. The smooth-curve relative-dimension lemma applies because $C$ is integral, separated, finite type and of dimension one: it makes $C_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ smooth of relative dimension one. For every further field extension $K/E$, the fibre-product identity $(C_E)_K\cong C_K$ and geometric integrality of $C$ make $(C_E)_K$ integral. Thus $C_E$ is geometrically integral, in particular nonempty and integral. Its sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is therefore nonempty, so smooth relative dimension one gives dimension one. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,E$ and its spectrum has one point); the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma gives that $C_E$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); relative dimension interpreted by definition-smooth-relative-dimension.

proof.text: Apply relative ampleness under base change with $X=C$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $T'=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and the given $L$. The only nonempty affine open of $T$ is $T$ itself, so its hypothesis is exactly ampleness of $L$; the conclusion on the whole affine $T'$ says that $L_E$ is ample. Pulling back a local rank-one trivialization of $L$ gives a rank-one trivialization of $L_E$, by the pullback formula, so $L_E$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0893 (lemma-ample-base-change); invertibility is local rank-one triviality and the pullback formula.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal V$ be finite locally free on $C_E$ and let $\mathcal I$ be a coherent ideal. On a trivializing affine open, $\mathcal V$ is the sheaf associated to $A^r$, so it is quasi-coherent and of finite type. The coherence criterion on the locally Noetherian scheme $C_E$ makes $\mathcal V$ coherent and makes $\mathcal I$ quasi-coherent of finite type. Locally where $\mathcal V\cong\mathcal O^r$, the map $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$ identifies $\mathcal I^{\oplus r}$ with $\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal V$, with inverse $a\otimes\sum_i b_ie_i\mapsto(b_ia)_i$. A finite direct sum of local presentations $\widetilde M$ is $\widetilde{M^{\oplus r}}$, and a finite list of generators for $M$ gives one for $M^{\oplus r}$. Hence this tensor is quasi-coherent of finite type, and the same criterion makes it coherent. This also covers rank zero.

source.place: Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), applied to finite local free modules and to the explicitly identified finite direct sums of a coherent ideal.

proof.text: Now fix an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$ and put $D=C_\Omega$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is an fpqc singleton covering. The bijection in fpqc descent of morphisms is in particular injective on $\operatorname{Hom}_F(C,C)$. Consequently equality of two base-changed automorphisms of $D$ implies equality of the original automorphisms of $C$. The injective homomorphism $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_F(C)$ therefore stays injective after base change. In particular $g_\Omega\ne\operatorname{id}_D$ whenever $g\ne1$.

source.place: Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful), last sentence, for a field-extension singleton fpqc covering; topologies.tex Tags 022B and 03L7.

proof.text: For each $g\ne1$, write $a=g_\Omega$ and form $Z_g=D\times_{D\times_\Omega D}D$ using $(\operatorname{id}_D,a)$ on the first factor and the diagonal on the second. Its projection $i_g:Z_g\to D$ is a closed immersion: it is a base change of the closed diagonal of the separated $D/\Omega$. The two fibre-product projection identities give $a\circ i_g=i_g$. For any $t:T\to D$, the fibre-product universal property says that $t$ factors through $i_g$ if and only if $a\circ t=t$ (the other component of a lift is then $t$). Thus this construction detects fixed geometric morphisms, including their residue-field maps, rather than just equality of underlying points.

source.place: Tag 01KM (lemma-where-are-they-equal), its displayed fibre-product construction; closedness follows by the definition of separatedness and Tag 01QR (morphisms-lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: The closed image $|Z_g|\subseteq|D|$ is proper. Indeed, if its image were all of $D$, then $i_g$ would have dense image. Apply the reduced-source separated-target equality lemma to $T=Y=D$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $W=Z_g$, $h=i_g$ and the two maps $a,\operatorname{id}_D$. The hypotheses hold because $D$ is integral, hence reduced, its structure morphism is separated, both maps are over $\Omega$, and they agree after $i_g$. The lemma would imply $a=\operatorname{id}_D$, contradicting faithfulness. The nonempty integral $D$ is irreducible. For completeness, a finite union of these proper closed subsets is proper by induction: the empty union is proper because $D$ is nonempty. If a proper closed union $A$ together with another proper closed subset $B$ covered $D$, irreducibility would force $A=D$ or $B=D$, contradicting their properness. Therefore $D^\circ=D\setminus\bigcup_{g\ne1}|Z_g|$ is nonempty and open. If a geometric point in $D^\circ$ were fixed by $g\ne1$, the factorization just established would put its image in $|Z_g|$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 01KM (lemma-where-are-they-equal), the reduced-source/dense-image consequence recorded in lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext; the finite-union induction is elementary irreducibility.

proof.text: Since $D$ is smooth over $\Omega$, density of closed points with finite separable residue field gives a closed $x\in D^\circ$ with $\kappa(x)/\Omega$ finite separable. Every element of this extension is algebraic; its irreducible minimal polynomial over the algebraically closed $\Omega$ has a root and is therefore linear. Hence $\kappa(x)=\Omega$ and $x$ gives an $\Omega$-rational geometric point. If two underlying orbit points $gx,hx$ were equal, their $\Omega$-rational point morphisms would coincide: a point with residue field $\Omega$ has just one residue-field map to $\Omega$ over $\Omega$. Composing with $h^{-1}$ would give a fixed geometric point for $h^{-1}g$, so $g=h$. Thus all $gx$ are distinct; they are closed and rational because $g$ is an $\Omega$-automorphism. When $G=\{1\}$ the union above is empty and $D^\circ=D$. No step divides by $|G|$ or assumes a characteristic restriction.

source.place: Tag 056U (lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense); algebraic closedness reduces the finite residue extension to the ground field, and orbit injectivity follows by the displayed group calculation.
